items.title: Time Reflection for Miro
items.summary: Exercise to get a high flight level view on your day to day to help you get visibility to make decisions
items.author: Joseph Hill
items.body:
## What it helps with

This interactive Miro template guides you through categorising your time into meaningful segments - whether it's deep work, meetings, personal care, family time, or other activities that matter to you. The visual nature of plotting these categories across a 24-hour period makes it immediately apparent how you're investing your time. Unlike traditional time tracking tools, this template creates an immediate visceral impact - you can literally see how your day fills up, making it impossible to ignore imbalances or overcrowding.

## Suggested workflow

1. Open the tool.
2. Follow the instructions

items.title: Job Reflection
items.summary: A simple exercise to gain impulses about how you are doing currently at work
items.author: Joseph Hill
items.body:
## When to use this

The simple prompt guides you through some questions based on helping you reflect your work over a defined period of time, after the reflection a JSON is created which you can use to create a report on how your work is going or use https://reflectify.squarecircletriangle.co/ to paste in to get a pre-filled report

## Prompt

You are guiding me through a structured reflection on my current job. Interview me one question at a time and wait for my answer before moving to the next question. Keep your tone warm and encouraging, and keep questions concise.

Step 1: Ask what language I'd like to use for this reflection (e.g. English, German, Spanish, French). From that point on, ask every question in that language, and write every piece of prose in your final JSON output - headline, summary, analyses, quotes, conclusion, etc. - in that language too. Keep the JSON keys themselves in English exactly as specified below, regardless of the chosen language.
Step 2: Ask how many months I want this reflection to cover (e.g. 3, 6, 12).
Step 3: Ask my job title.

Then run a guided interview covering, roughly in this order:
1. Achievements & wins - what am I proud of in this period?
2. Regrets or missed opportunities - what would I do differently?
3. Challenges I faced and how I handled them
4. Skills I grew - ask me to name 4-6 skills and rate my growth in each from 0-100
5. Relationships & collaboration - who did I work well with, any friction worth noting?
6. Energy & wellbeing - how has my energy/burnout trended? Ask for a 0-100 score and a short note
7. Goals for the next period

Ask thoughtful follow-up questions where it helps, but keep the whole interview reasonably tight - no more than a few questions per topic.

When the interview is complete, respond with ONLY a single JSON code block (no other text before or after) that exactly matches this schema:

{
  "jobTitle": "string",
  "periodMonths": number,
  "overallScore": number, // 0-100, your holistic assessment of how the period went
  "headline": "string", // one punchy sentence summing up the period
  "summary": "string", // 2-4 sentence summary
  "achievements": [{ "title": "string", "detail": "string" }],
  "achievementsAnalysis": "string", // 2-3 sentences analyzing the pattern across my achievements - what they reveal about me
  "regrets": [{ "title": "string", "detail": "string" }],
  "regretsAnalysis": "string", // 2-3 sentences analyzing the pattern across my regrets
  "skills": [{ "name": "string", "level": number }], // 0-100
  "skillsAnalysis": "string", // 2-3 sentences on what my skill growth (or stagnation) suggests
  "timeline": [{ "label": "string", "detail": "string" }], // chronological milestones across the period
  "quotes": ["string"], // 2-4 short first-person quotes pulled from my answers, verbatim where possible
  "goals": [{ "title": "string", "detail": "string" }],
  "goalsAnalysis": "string", // 2-3 sentences on whether these goals address what came up in the interview
  "wellbeing": { "score": number, "note": "string" }, // optional, include if we discussed it
  "sentiment": {
    "label": "string", // one or two words, e.g. "Mostly positive", "Mixed", "Strained"
    "score": number, // -100 (very negative) to 100 (very positive), your read of my overall tone across all answers
    "note": "string" // one sentence on what drives that read
  },
  "conclusion": "string" // 2-3 sentence closing reflection tying the period together and pointing forward
}

Base every analysis field on genuine patterns in my actual answers, not generic advice. Before writing the final JSON, review each analysis field (achievementsAnalysis, regretsAnalysis, skillsAnalysis, goalsAnalysis, sentiment.note, conclusion) and confirm it references a specific detail from my answers rather than a generic observation that could apply to anyone; rewrite any field that fails this check.

Save that JSON as a .json file (for example reflection.json) so I can upload it to my reflection report tool.

items.title: Retrospective Builder for Miro
items.summary: Simple Miro Template for Quickly building Retrospectives
items.author: Joseph Hill
items.body:
## What it helps with

The simple to use Miro template enables you to build out the stages of a retrospective with various pre-defined panels, so that you in a matter of minutes can piece together an effective retrospective

## Suggested workflow

1. Open the tool.
2. Click on Use Template
3. Go through each stage of the Retrospective and add the panels which match your needs
4. Share the link with your team
5. Execute the retrospective

items.title: Self Impressions & Reflections
items.summary: A simple method to engage in 1:1 feedback in a productive and effective manner
items.author: Joseph Hill
items.body:
## What it helps with

One interesting activity which should be done once every couple of years is the Self Reflection & Impressions activity. It is an intimate, honest and transparent approach to getting to know a fellow team member better and to have an understanding about them as a person.

NOTE: Please do not force people to do this, but it should be something both parties are open to

## Suggested workflow

1. Find someone who wants to participate 2. Print 4x this page (One for you evaluate yourself One for you to evaluate the other person One for them to evaluate themselves One for them to evaluate you)
2. Engage in a meeting and both evaluate yourselves 4. Evaluate each other (allow around 5 minutes)
3. Decide which person should go first
4. Discuss when you both have conflicting ranges
5. Switch person and repeat

items.title: Rapid LDJ for Miro
items.summary: Simple yet effective approach to minimise big discussions and have an outcome at the end of a session
items.author: Joseph Hill
items.body:
## What it helps with

The Miro template creates a simple tool called Lightning Decision Jam which can be applied and utilised across a number of different contexts and is very helpful to reduce large group discussions which usually do not result in an outcome. 

I have used this in a 30min session in a previous company to define a backend teams full year roadmap

## Suggested workflow

1. Open the tool.
2. Click on utilise the template
3. Follow the moderation guide on the template

items.title: Breadboarding for Miro

items.author: Joseph Hill
items.body:
## What it helps with

Breadboarding is a very simple process where you map all the user interactions on each screen and may the outcome. The approach is inspired my electrical breadboards, which are used to test out circuit designs before building them. 

You will find gaps and UX improvements along the way of breadboarding your product or feature

## Suggested workflow

1. Open the tool.
2. Follow the instructions in the template

items.author: Joseph Hill
items.body:
## Why it is worth reading

The book really helped me to understand the different flight levels in an organisation, how to connect the details to the high-level and really helped me to understand how to communicate as you can define which flight level someone is at. The book's design is really easy reading and serves as a nice pick up reference book. I would recommend for anyone managing a team or process as it enables you to gain different perspectives

## Best for

Product Management and Leadership Roles

## Key takeaway

When you understanding different perspectives relating to different flight levels, you gain a better understanding on HOW and WHAT you can communicate with WHO and how to structure your working mode and practices for the different flight levels

items.title: Future Product Days
items.summary: Future Product Days is a three-day conference in Copenhagen for professionals working in digital product design, UX, engineering, leadership and AI.
items.author: Joseph Hill
items.body:
## Why it is worth attending

Future Product Days is worth attending for Product Managers who want to stay ahead of developments in product strategy, UX, technology and AI. The conference offers practical insights from experienced industry leaders, hands-on workshops and opportunities to learn how other organisations approach product challenges. It is also a valuable place to expand your professional network, exchange ideas with peers and return with new methods that can be applied directly to your products and teams.

## Best for

Best suited to Product Managers, Product Owners, UX and design professionals, engineering leaders and product executives working on digital products. It will be especially valuable for those looking to strengthen their product strategy, explore practical uses of AI, improve cross-functional collaboration and learn from peers facing similar challenges.

## What to expect

Expect a mix of inspiring talks, practical workshops and discussions covering product strategy, UX, leadership, engineering and AI. The most valuable takeaway is likely to be a clearer understanding of how strong product teams turn customer needs, emerging technology and business goals into better product decisions.

items.title: The Bottle Analogy
items.summary: Understand how to present your thoughts and opinions to a mixed level group
items.author: Joseph Hill
items.body:
## Why it is worth reading

The simple approach explains how to enable better group discussions around topics, in a group of mixed level thinkers. Once you understand the concept, you can easily apply it to a number of aspects of your daily work.

## Best for

Anyone who needs to get value from group think or wants to drive a direction forward with bringing people along with them

## Key takeaway

Understanding that humans when presented with a concrete idea or concept can better articulate their thoughts, opinions and ideas instead of a blank piece of paper where everything is possible and discussions go all in different directions.

items.title: Indexes for Metrics
items.summary: Using indexes to develop high level health metrics which can be used to drive goal orientated development
items.author: Joseph Hill
items.body:
## Why it is worth reading

The article explains on how simplifying complicated metrics into simple 0 - 100 indexes enables all experience levels and perspectives to clearly see WHERE we are right now and opens the door to define WHAT is the standard we want to push for, and then measure it again after a period of time to see if we improved the metric or not

## Best for

Product Management and Leadership to bring higher level metrics and understanding across a broad and mixed knowledge group

## Key takeaway

Simplifying and grouping metrics into multiple 0 - 100 health metrics brings a lot of value and enables positive discussions into WHERE we want to get to
